target_customer: Consumers who want to clip and share video from any website
problem: People could not easily save and share a short moment from video on any site, only from specific platforms.
business_model: Consumer product aiming at a content network; no revenue model documented

founders.name: Neil Joglekar
founders.background_notes: Confirmed the seed round to TechCrunch in September 2012 and is listed on the YC page.

exit.reason: No company statement found; the cause is not public.

competitors.name: ClipClock
competitors.what: Let users start YouTube or Vimeo videos at a chosen moment, comment and share
competitors.traction_then: Nine employees and an iPhone app in fall 2012
competitors.funding_then: $750K seed, $2M round said to be on the way

technical_complexity.rationale: Clipping video from arbitrary websites needed a bookmarklet and handling many embed formats, moderately hard for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Any video site or social app could add clipping, and ClipClock offered a similar product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google updated the YouTube editor in 2012 per a trade report; no source shows direct copying of ReelSurfer.

market_need_then: Online video sharing was growing in 2012, but sources give no usage figures for ReelSurfer.

branding.domain_note: Used reelsurfer.com; the site returned a service error at fetch time.

brand_strength.rationale: TechCrunch and The Next Web covered the seed round and product updates, but no source shows community or viral spread.

outcome_analysis: ReelSurfer raised an $880K seed in September 2012 and shipped profiles and commenting through autumn 2012, but the directory lists it as Inactive and no post-mortem exists. A startup data site dates the end to 2015, unverified. The cause is not public; a crowded clipping field and platform copying are possible but unsupported.
notes: TechCrunch body says $880K while its social summary says $900K, and The Next Web said close to $900,000 (seen in search results only). Round rests on TechCrunch plus that second outlet snippet. A startup data site claims a 2012 to 2015 life and about $1.3M cash burned; unverified AI generated summary, not used as a round. Dealroom marks the company closed. A Crunchbase page exists but its figures were not opened.
